rationale:
Verdict: 10 of the 18 fix-self-decide rulings landed cleanly and are confirmed against the code; 8 landed only in part, plus the implementation half of the owner's counter ruling; 8 new findings stand; 5 items are nitpicks and are dismissed by name. Nothing found this round reopens a §2 decision, and nothing needs the owner: every surviving item is a text edit inside a section the implementer owns, and each one names the step it gates. So §13 steps 3-8 may start, on the same discipline the rev-5 report used — each item lands in the plan before the step that consumes it.

What gates step 3 (must land first): the three unwritten step-3 test breakages under `test-mapping-not-implementable` (test_interpretation_driver.py:32 imports `_local_task`, which §15.1 deletes, and mcp:25 / codex:48 import from that module, so all three test modules fail at COLLECTION — exactly the defect class the ruling was written to end), and new finding D, the step-3 write channel. D is the one place where the rev-5 report's own prescription turned out to be incomplete, and I say so plainly: the ruling ordered `inv_fields` replaced by `recs` on the ground that "phase 1 already writes its mint back into recs[i]". I checked semantic_interpretation.py:940-959 — the write-back at :957-959 happens ONLY in the digest-mismatch branch. The two epsilon branches (:944-951) leave recs[i] untouched and carry their number in `version_to_write` alone, and `interpreted_at` never rides `recs` at all: write_answer reads the PAIR `inv_fields[task_idx]` at :386-388, whose second half is `ia_snapshot` (:1131). So after step 3 the writer has no source for interpreted_at and no source for epsilon on two of three branches. The honest repair is to keep the scan's pair as a step-3-only field and delete it at step 4 when `_EffStar` + `rec_cache` take over.

What gates steps 4-5: the dry-path refresh crash (new finding C — item 6's "over every entry" dereferences `rec.expr` for an uncached entry, where get_many yields None; today's guard is reachable only under `cached and not stale` with an `assert rec is not None` right above it, semantic_interpretation.py:1125-1129, and §15.10's new dry-refresh test quotes 0, so it cannot catch this); the four sites still asserting "a dry run writes nothing", one of which (§10:618) the ruling named in terms; `working_names` (new finding B); the per-theory store resolution with no failure path (new finding A — `_conn_semantic_vector_store` calls `_resolve_embedding_config`, which warns and then `raise RuntimeError` at semantics.py:2779 in exactly the unconfigured case D2 says must degrade quietly, so as written every theory dies where D2 promises the judge decides alone); the two `prefilter_disabled` locations; and the counter derivations.

On severity calibration: I decline V2's "blocker" label on finding A. It is a real D2 violation, but it is one missing `except` clause in a paragraph the implementer writes at step 5, it announces itself on the first unconfigured run, and D2 already fixes the answer — the same discount the rev-5 report applied to items whose failure is total, immediate and self-announcing.

On the pattern worth naming: three verifiers independently rediscovered the same defect from different directions (the run-scoped-state cluster: `prefilter_disabled` on the task vs on RunState, the throw-away RunState, §5.4 step 2's stale store sentence), which is a sign that §15.8's run-scoped-state paragraph is the least finished part of the plan, not that three separate things are wrong; I merged them where they are one edit and kept them apart where they are not. The residual habits to watch are re-filing something the previous judge already dismissed (the `_BATCH_SIZE` fixture scope was dropped by the rev-5 filter as tests-8 and came back unchanged) and mining a grep recipe for two more hits when installing that recipe was the whole point of the ruling.

not_landed.fix: Three step-3 breakages are still unwritten, and the one instruction that did land is filed against the wrong file. In §15.10's driver bullet add: `_local_task` is imported at test_interpretation_driver.py:32 and set at :138, :192, :441 — it goes away with the ContextVar, `_answer` goes through `mk_answer_tool(task).handler`, and `_run` passes the task explicitly (`await _run_agent(make_driver, task)`; today `_run_agent(make_driver)` at :139 and :445). Because test_interpretation_mcp_server.py:25 and test_interpretation_codex.py:48 both import `_make_task` from that module, leaving this unwritten takes all three modules down at collection. In the mcp bullet add: delete `task.batch_range = task.batches[0][1]` (:86, inside a test §15.10 keeps), and say the four session registrations at :96, :137, :154, :155 pass `mk_answer_tool(task)`. Move the `batch_range` sentence out of the driver bullet (plan:1229-1230): the only other occurrence, driver:181, is inside the very test plan:1233-1235 replaces, so as filed it applies to nothing.

The dry branch, §6.3, §11 and §15.10 were updated; four sites still assert the opposite, one of them named in the required fix. Edit §5.2:150 ("Read-only; nothing minted, nothing written") and §5.2:169 ("no write") to say the dry run's only write is the statement refresh — no gate field, no mint, no counter put; edit §5.3.2:258 to say the LIVE-path refresh moves after the LLM work while the dry path keeps its own before the early return; and replace §10:618 ("dry run returns the seed count, writes nothing, exact at zero") with the case that would have caught the loss, as the ruling ordered. Then narrow item 6 per new finding C.

Half (b) landed in the prose and not in the blueprint: §5.4:299 and §15.8:1188-1196 put the flag on `RunState`, but §15.3:869 still has `self.prefilter_disabled = emb_store is None` on the per-theory `InterpretationTask` and §15.5:986 still writes `task.prefilter_disabled = True`. With one task per theory and theories concurrent under `schedule_dag`, the §15 half reproduces exactly the defect the ruling upheld: one #5 line and one 60 s timeout per theory. Delete `prefilter_disabled` from §15.3 (keep `emb_store`, whose None-ness is a legitimate per-theory fact); in §15.5 make the skip test `task.emb_store is None or run_state.prefilter_disabled`, and set `run_state.prefilter_disabled = True` BEFORE `await _report(..., warn=True)` — the ordering half of the ruled fix, which is stated in §5.4 and nowhere in §15.

#13 and #16 landed (#13 is monotone: `enqueue` fires only on a `_NOT_ENROLLED` entry, plan:824-825, 1038, 1074; #16 carries D7's "(or more)" and drops the unqualified "and up to date"). #14 and #15 did not: §12:709-713 defines m run-wide, while §15.3:878-879 says the three retry texts carry today's numbers "unchanged" and §15.4:928 feeds them `task.unanswered_in_batch()`. Followed literally, the stall line prints the batch's count over a now theory-wide denominator — verbatim the "1 of 244" falsehood the review flagged. Two things must land in §15.8 beside the addressing rule: the derivations (N = count(state != _NOT_ENROLLED), k = count(state in {_GATING, _DONE}) — the ruling's numerator clause, not `_DONE` alone, which with the 40-session cap would leave the only fine-grained sign of life near zero for minutes — and m = count(state in {_QUEUED, _SENT})), and the statement that `_retry_unanswered` passes the run-wide unanswered set to BOTH `retry_report` and `unanswered_failure` (so the give-up line's names and its m are one set) while the chunk it re-asks stays `unanswered_in_batch()`. Drop "unchanged" from §15.3:878-879: the wording is unchanged, the numbers are not. While editing, give #16's legend its own letters — §12 currently uses N for "entries enrolled so far" at :702-704 and for "the theory's entity count" at :714.

The loop conversion landed with jitter, the capped exponential on the RateLimitError arm only, no give-up arm and no budget consumption — but it dropped the budget increment. Today `depth` IS the recycle budget: the two throttle arms re-enter with `depth` (semantic_interpretation.py:822, 827) and the two recycle arms with `depth + 1` (:841, :862) against the `depth >= _MAX_AGENT_RECYCLES` guards at :834 and :855. §15.4:920-921's "a handler `continue`s" loses that increment, which silently unbounds poisoned-session and transient recycling. Add one clause: `depth` becomes a local incremented in exactly the two recycle arms and left alone by the two throttle arms, so `_MAX_AGENT_RECYCLES` keeps its meaning.

The preferred route landed in §15.8 (`server.gate_emb_store` gone, per-connection resolution, D16's `warn` threaded one hop further), but §5.4 step 2 was not brought along: plan:273-276 still says `store` is "the `Semantic_Vector_Store` the startup check resolved once per run". The startup check runs on the cone-root connection and cone-root `cfg_context` (plan:399-400), so a store resolved there and reused by every theory is precisely the D5 violation the ruling removed — and an implementer following §5.4, the normative description of the step, rebuilds it. Rewrite that clause as "the `Semantic_Vector_Store` this `interpret_file` resolved on its own connection (§15.8)", and add one clause to §5.6 saying the startup check's provider is constructed to validate the configuration and then discarded.

§15.4:931-939 carries the replacement warrant in full, including the optional structural clause. §5.3.1:209-211 still reads "so today's retry loop, `batch_remaining` and the completeness invariant are unchanged" — the exact sentence the ruling named alongside §15.4 — so the plan asserts the retired property in one section and its new warrant in another, and §11:663 sends the implementer to §5.3.1 for a restatement that lives in §15.4. Replace §5.3.1's clause with "`task.results[i] is None` iff queued or sent, so today's retry loop and `batch_remaining` are unchanged; the completeness invariant keeps its shape but not its warrant (§15.4)", and repoint §11:663 at §15.4.

The §15.5 half landed exactly as ruled (`judged` and `has_gate_fields` each defined once and keyed on the digest, the parenthetical rewritten, `_TRACKED_KINDS` gone with a positive statement that it is not defined). The token discipline outside that block did not: plan:959 still calls the digest predicate `tracked` inside `_gate` (a second name for `judged`), and §15.8 item 4 at plan:1150 still calls the digest-or-deps predicate `tracked` — the predicate §15.5 has just renamed `has_gate_fields` while citing that very code line. So §15 now has two names for one predicate and one name for two, one subsection apart, which is the collision the ruling set out to remove; §0's glossary (plan:22) sides with :959 against :1150. Use `judged` at plan:959, and rewrite item 4 as `has_gate_fields = digest or deps`, noting that semantic_interpretation.py:1101 calls it `tracked` today. Wording only.

The bound, the constant, §5.4's sentence and the test all landed, and the placement is correct against the real code (the ladder's handler is `except Exception` at semantic_embedding.py:355, so the timeout's cancellation cannot be swallowed, and the resulting `TimeoutError` is caught unchanged by §15.5's `except Exception` behind `_gate`'s `except asyncio.CancelledError: raise`). One residue: §15.5:981-986, the `_prefilter` block an implementer copies, spells out the two renderings, the one `embed` call, the cosine and the failure path and never mentions the timeout — while the ruling put the bound "inside `_prefilter`". Add the `async with asyncio.timeout(_PREFILTER_TIMEOUT_S)` line to that block. Wording only; §15 is declared the blueprint, so the bound belongs where the code is written.

new_findings_upheld.title: The per-theory `semantic_vector_store()` resolution has no failure path, so an unconfigured embedding service fails every theory instead of skipping the prefilter (D2)
new_findings_upheld.fix: Confirmed in code: §15.8:1197-1200 and item 7:1161-1163 resolve and pass `emb_store` with no guard and no `except`, but `_conn_semantic_vector_store` (semantics.py:2792-2812) calls `_resolve_embedding_config`, which warns and then `raise RuntimeError(msg)` at semantics.py:2779 whenever the whole default triple is in force with no API key — the unconfigured case §12 #4 exists for; `embedding_config.dimension` adds a second raising path through `Embedding_Provider.__init__`. Both propagate out of `interpret_file` and, through the gate task group, fail the theory — after the startup check has already printed #4 and promised the run continues. §15.8 must say: `interpret_file` skips the resolution when `current_run_state().prefilter_disabled` is already set, and otherwise wraps it in `except Exception -> emb_store = None` with a host-log line only (#4 was printed once by the startup check, D16). Add one §10 bullet: an unconfigured embedding service completes the run with every gate judged and no error.

new_findings_upheld.title: `working_names` is a snapshot of the seed set, so an entity enrolled later is queryable and its stale stored text can be copied back as the fresh interpretation
new_findings_upheld.fix: The rejection half of `on-answer-not-enrolled` landed cleanly and keyed on state; this is a consequence of its second half. §15.8:1182-1184 narrows `working_names` to "the enrolled entries' names" but never says the enrolled set grows. In code the list is built once (`working_names = [e.name for e in task.entries]`, semantic_interpretation.py:1191) and closed over by `mk_query_by_name_tool` (semantics.py:1717); every dependent a CHANGED verdict enrols afterwards (plan:1038) is absent from it, so the query tool hands the agent the stored English text of an entity it is at that moment being asked to re-interpret — and the refusal message at semantics.py:1756-1761 says "it is or will be your task", i.e. names exactly the case the plan now drops. The leak points at the gate: an agent that answers with the text it was just shown produces a near-identical fresh text, the prefilter passes, the judge says "same", and a genuinely changed entity is written UNCHANGED and never mints. Make the enrolled-name list an attribute of `InterpretationTask`, appended to by `enqueue`, and hand `mk_query_by_name_tool` that same mutable list object — the membership test re-reads it on every call, so nothing else changes. Extend §15.10's unrequested-answer test with the mirror case: after a CHANGED verdict enrols a dependent, `query` must refuse that dependent's name.

new_findings_upheld.title: The dry-path statement refresh runs "over every entry" and dereferences an absent record, so a dry run of any theory containing a new entity raises AttributeError
new_findings_upheld.fix: This is a defect in the text written to satisfy `statement-refresh-lost-at-zero`, not in the ruling. §15.8 item 6 (plan:1155-1160) runs item 8's refresh "over every entry" on the dry path, and item 8's guard is today's verbatim `if e.prop_str and rec.expr != e.prop_str`. In the code that guard is reachable only under `if cached and not stale:` with `assert rec is not None` immediately above it (semantic_interpretation.py:1125-1129), and `recs` comes from `get_many`, which yields None for an absent key. The widening also buys nothing: the case the fix exists for is a cone whose only difference is a printed `prop_str`, which has an empty seed set by construction, so every entry is already in item 8's own `_NOT_ENROLLED` set; a seed's `expr` is rewritten by the live run that interprets it anyway. Delete "over every entry" and let the dry path run item 8's set unchanged (`state[i] == _NOT_ENROLLED`, equivalently the scan's `cached and not stale`, where `rec` is provably non-None), saying in one clause why that set is also "entries this run did not write" on the dry path. §15.10:1268-1270's new test quotes 0 and therefore has no uncached entry, so it cannot catch this: add one uncached entry to it.

new_findings_upheld.title: §15.11 step 3's write channel supplies neither the scan's frozen epsilon nor `interpreted_at`, so step 3 as specified cannot write and its "behaviour equals today's" claim is false
new_findings_upheld.fix: The rev-5 ruling's premise is accurate only for one of three branches, and I verified this: `inv_fields` is a PAIR (`(version_to_write.get(i), ia_snapshot.get(i))`, semantic_interpretation.py:1177-1178) that `write_answer` unpacks at :386-391; phase 1 writes back into `recs[i]` only in the digest-mismatch branch (:957-959), while the two epsilon branches (:944-951) leave `recs[i]` untouched and carry their number in `version_to_write` alone; and `recs[i].interpreted_at` is the OLD stored snapshot, not the eff* the scan computed at :1131. The step-4/5 successors (`_EffStar`, `task.rec_cache`) arrive one and two steps later, and today's `eff_value` is a closure local to `interpret_file`, so a task method cannot call it either. Fix in §13 step 3 and §15.11: keep the scan's pair as a step-3-only task field alongside `recs` and delete it at step 4 when `_EffStar` + `rec_cache` take over — then step 3 really does write "the scan's fields" and the equality with today's behaviour holds. If instead the implementer pulls `_EffStar` forward into step 3, §15.11 must drop "behaviour equals today's" and say that version and interpreted_at are now read at write time (higher, conservative: over-signalling and lower snapshots), because at step 3 the scan still mints and concurrent sibling bumps are live — which is the case parent write-back discipline 4 exists for.

new_findings_upheld.title: `current_run_state()` returning a fresh throw-away `RunState` per access makes "once per run" false on exactly the path the tests use
new_findings_upheld.fix: Plan:1194-1196 makes the unlocked fallback a NEW object on every call, so `prefilter_disabled` never sticks off the lock: the prefilter is retried per entity, each retry can burn the full 60 s timeout, and text §12 #5 prints once per failing entity, not once per run. §15.10's new test file drives `interpret_file` directly over an isolated store and never takes the lock, and §10:596 asserts "embedding failure => prefilter skipped, judge alone" — an assertion this fallback cannot satisfy. The locked path is sound and its ownership argument checks out (one FileLock holder per database directory, one directory per host process). Make one run own one object with or without the lock: resolve `current_run_state()` once at the top of `interpret_file`, or have the caller create the `RunState` and pass it down beside `emb_store`, and state that off the lock the scope degrades to one `interpret_file`. A per-access fresh object must not be the fallback, and neither may a never-cleared module-level singleton — that is the stale-across-runs shape the `gate-emb-store-on-server` ruling rejected.

new_findings_upheld.title: §3's decision table has no row for a WIP theorem collection or method, and its theorem-alike row as qualified contradicts §15.5
new_findings_upheld.fix: Confirmed against the ML: `attach` emits `(..., NONE, [])` for an entry whose `Semantic_Digest.semantics_of` returns NONE (semantic_store.ML:1798-1800), and `mk_prop_str` handles `Theorem_Collection` and `Method` as WIP kinds (:711-712). Such an entry has no digest AND no deps, so it matches neither §3's "theorem-alike (WIP)" row (whose only qualifier is "`semantic_digest` None", and which promises version "stored, else ε" and interpreted_at eff*) nor the "persistent theory" row — yet §3 declares its rows mutually exclusive and the rev-5 ruling on `write-ia-clobbers-persistent` explicitly extended that path to cover collections and methods. Only §15.5:998-1000 records the truth (all gate fields None, today's behaviour). Either add a row ("WIP collection / method: no digest, no deps -> None everywhere") or extend the theorem-alike row's qualifier to "(`semantic_digest` None, deps present; with no deps every gate field is None)", and add the case beside the theorem-alike and persistent bullets in §10's decision-table entry (plan:593-594) so the test family covers it.

new_findings_upheld.title: §5.4 opens with "no concurrency limit" and its step 3 never names `_JUDGE_SESSIONS`, contradicting D12 in the very section D12 points at
new_findings_upheld.fix: D12 (plan:63) puts "a process-wide `asyncio.Semaphore(40)` around §5.4 step 3 only", and §15.1:784 / §15.6:1118-1120 / §10:607 carry it — but §5.4:263-264 still says the gate tasks run with "no concurrency limit" and step 3 (plan:284-287) never mentions a permit. The two statements are reconcilable (the gate TASKS are unbounded; only the judge session inside step 3 takes a permit), but §5.4 is the normative description an implementer reads first and it currently reads as the opposite of a settled decision. Rewrite the clause as "one asyncio task per entity ...; the gate tasks themselves are unbounded, and only the judge session of step 3 takes a permit from `_JUDGE_SESSIONS` (D12)", and name the semaphore in step 3. One sentence of justification is worth having there: a task waiting for a permit never holds one, and the loop's wake-up comes from `gate_finished`, so the cap cannot deadlock the queue.

new_findings_upheld.title: The gate-group unwrap can log-and-drop a `BaseException` leaf and has no defined empty-leaves case
new_findings_upheld.fix: This corrects the rev-5 report's own wording, which said "catch `BaseExceptionGroup`", and the plan followed it verbatim at :313-316. CPython's TaskGroup raises a plain `ExceptionGroup` when every collected error is an `Exception` and a `BaseExceptionGroup` only when a base error was collected — so the `Base` half of the catch adds exactly the groups that must not be reduced to `raise leaves[0] from None` plus log lines, since a dropped `SystemExit` / `KeyboardInterrupt` leaf is a swallow, which D10 forbids. Catch `ExceptionGroup`, so a group carrying a base error propagates untouched, and say that an empty filtered list re-raises the group unchanged (with CancelledError leaves never entering `_errors`, that arm is defensive, but `leaves[0]` on an empty list is an IndexError masking the real failure). Two tokens and one clause; no behaviour change on any reachable path.

dismissed: §11's site list is narrower than §11's own grep (semantic_store.ML:1866-1869 and Test/Test_All.thy:146-147). Both sites exist and both state the retired equality — but the rev-5 ruling upheld `doc-list-omits-load-bearing-statements` precisely BECAUSE the old recipe ("search for the dry run's `n`") reached none of them, and the ruling's fix was to install a grep over metering / quote / actual work / by construction / would be asked. I ran it: it finds both. §13 step 8 now tells the implementer to find the sites that way, "not by line number", so the list in §11 is an aid and not a manifest. Mining the newly installed recipe for two more hits and filing them as a residue of the ruling that installed it is a nitpick.

`_make_task` mutating `SI._BATCH_SIZE` with a module-scoped autouse fixture. This is tests-8, which the rev-5 filter already dropped by name, with the same two supporting facts (no conftest.py exists; two other modules import `_make_task`) and the same consequence: a fixable test-suite annoyance, not a defect in the implementation being planned. Re-filing a dismissed item unchanged is what the nitpick rule is for.

§15.10 lists test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py twice (plan:1220-1222 untagged, plan:1250-1255 tagged "(step 3)" and strictly larger). A duplicated bullet from the edit that added the two new cases; zero implementation consequence, since the tagged copy subsumes the untagged one word for word. Delete plan:1220-1222 while making the other edits — it does not need a finding.

§15.6:1083-1085 "contradicts itself" about `_MAX_STALLED_RETRIES`. It says the constant is read by `_retry_unanswered` and then, in the same sentence, that `max_stalled_retries` is the attribute `_retry_unanswered` reads, with "(interpretation: `_MAX_STALLED_RETRIES`; judge: 1)" spelled out immediately. The disambiguation is right there, the constant is genuinely also read for the "attempt <i> of 10" text, and the compensating line the ruling required (the attribute carries two meanings) is present. Reading the loose half of a sentence against its own next clause is a nitpick.

§12 reusing the letter N for two quantities (#13-#15 "entries enrolled so far", #16 "the theory's entity count"). Real, and against §0's one-word-per-concept rule, but it is a plan-side legend and not user-visible text — the printed lines carry numbers, not letters — and each line's legend is local and complete. Not worth a finding of its own; I folded the disambiguation into the `user-visible-counters-rebased` fix, where the derivations are being written anyway.
